Heard learned counsel for the appellants, Sri Mohan Kant Baghel, learned counsel for the informant/opposite party no.2, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State of U.P. and perused the record.

These criminal appeals under Section 14-A(2) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act hav been preferred by the appellants Dev Kumar and Anil Kumar with the prayer to set aside the bail rejection orders dated 24.02.2023 and 17.03.2023 passed by learned Special Judge (SC/ST Act), Firozabad in Bail Application Nos. 501 of 2023 and 879 of 2023, arising Dev Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82473712/
1 out of Complaint Case No. 109 of 2019, under Sections 406, 420, 323, 354, 504, 506 I.P.C. &
Sections 3 (1) (Da) (Dha) of SC/ST Act, Police Station South, District Firozabad.
Learned counsel for the appellants argued that the appellants are innocent and they have been falsely implicated in this case.

sentences.text: Initially the opposite party no.2/informant filed an application under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C. before the court concerned against the appellants and others with the allegations that on 08.02.2017, appellants took a sum of Rs.30,000/- from her for the purpose of delivery.
They did not return the aforesaid money to her.

Thereafter, they again took Rs. 50,000/-
from her.
When she asked them to return total amount of Rs. 80,000/-, on 23.04.2019, appellants alongwith other co-accused forcibly entered into her house and committed mar-peet with her by lathi and danda.
She was also threatened and abused by them by her caste related words.
On the basis of aforesaid application a complaint case was registered against the appellants.

It is further submitted that there are material contradictions in the version of complaint as well as the statements of complainant and other witnesses recorded under Section 200 and 202 Cr.P.C. and the appellants were illegally summoned by the court concerned to face trial vide order dated 21.11.2019.
It is further submitted that dispute is purely civil in nature.
It is further submitted that there is no medical report of opposite party no.2 to support the allegation made in the application under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C.
Lastly, it is submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that there is no chance of the appellants fleeing away from the judicial process or tampering with the prosecution evidence.

The appellants Devkumar and Anil Kumar are languishing in jail since 27.01.2023 and 28.02.2023 respectively and in case they are released on bail, they will not misuse the liberty of bail and will cooperate in the early disposal of the case.
Per contra, learned A.G.A. assisted by learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the aforesaid factual aspects of the matter.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions of learned counsel for the parties and keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, this Court is of the view that the appellants have made out a case for bail.
The Court below erred in rejecting the bail application.
The impugned order suffers from infirmity and illegality and the same is liable to be set-aside and the appeals are liable to be allowed.

Accordingly, the appeals are allowed and the impugned order rejecting the bail applications of the appellants are set-aside.
Let the appellants, namely, Dev Kumar and Anil Kumar involved in the above Case be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The appellants will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii) The appellants will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witness.

2 (iii) The appellants will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

sentences.text: (iv) The appellants shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which they are accused, or suspected, of the commission of which they are suspected.

(v) The appellants shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.
